record.label: production-branch reference; deployment unverified
record.scope: The three units in appliesTo declare ATTRACT: Milotic (3 stars), Swoobat (2 stars), Woobat (1 star). The strategy is shared; unit differences are the star count (target-count table index), range and maxPP. Units not listed are not covered.
record.summary: Spends PP and charms a number of randomly chosen enemy-team units (1/2/3/5 by stars) for a base 1000 ms each. It deals no damage and needs no target: because requiresTarget is false it is cast from the moving state as soon as PP is full. A charmed unit sets its target to the caster, walks toward it instead of acting and stops being able to attack normally while charmed.

targeting.who: up to nbTargets distinct units drawn at random from every board entity whose team differs from the caster's
targeting.note: The candidate filter reads board.cells without any range, targettable, alive or invisibility test, so the draw covers the whole board. If fewer candidates than nbTargets exist, all are charmed. Targets already charmed (or with rune protect) are drawn but triggerCharm does nothing for them, so a draw can be wasted.

geometry.shape: none; random selection over the whole board

effects.scaling: table[stars-1]; no AP or crit scaling
effects.resolution: applied = min(requested, number of enemy-team entities in board.cells); fewer are actually charmed when drawn units are already charmed or have rune protect

statusEffects.scaling: duration x (1 + caster AP/100) because apBoost is true; no star or crit scaling
statusEffects.resolution: applied duration = requested x (1 + AP/100), x1.3 in MISTY weather, then the target's SWIFT_SWIM (x0.7) / HYDRATION (x0.5) / WATER_VEIL or SURGE_SURFER (x0.3) reduction (one of them) and -10% per Odd Keystone on the target's player, with rounding in the reductions. Not applied if the target is already charmed or has rune protect. Effect while charmed: its target becomes the caster, it moves toward the caster until adjacent and does not attack from the attacking state; damage the target takes from the caster shortens the charm by 500 ms per hit; the charm ends when the remaining time runs out and the target is re-chosen.

starBehavior.note: The target count is indexed by the casting entity's stars; the 4-star value (5, also the ?? fallback) is not reachable by the bare factory star counts. Duration does not change with stars. Whether other mechanics raise an entity's star count was not examined.

record.positionalConditions: None in the strategy. The charm's effect on movement depends on distance to the caster (charmed units walk until within 1 cell).
record.repeatedCastsAndModes: No stored state or modes. Each cast spends maxPP of PP and redraws targets independently; a unit still charmed from an earlier cast is not recharmed (the timer is not extended).
record.rawVsResolved: Requested: 1/2/3 targets (1/2/3 stars) and 1000 ms charm. Applied charm duration per target = 1000 x (1 + AP/100), then weather and target-side reductions; targets that are already charmed receive nothing. No damage is dealt, so no takenDamage applies.
dependsOnUnverifiedGenericCombat: Which units sit in board.cells (dead units, bench, untargettable or invisible units) was not read: the board's cell storage and removal of dead entities were not traced

When the cast fires in a real fight (PP gain, silence, canCast) - only the pp >= maxPP && canCast gate and the moving-state requiresTarget=false branch were read; a unit that is already attacking and not in the moving state was not traced
How the charmed unit's movement is resolved (getMoveSpeed, pathing around obstacles) and what happens when canMove is false (the charmed unit then falls to the other branches) were not read
Crit resolution is irrelevant here (no crit-dependent value in the strategy); the crit flag is accepted but unused
unresolved: Whether dead units can remain in board.cells and be drawn as targets
Whether a target that is untargettable or banished can be charmed (no check in the strategy)
Why the strategy passes the attacker's AP into the duration (apBoost true) while SWEET_SCENT does not - a recorded difference, not an issue
Whether the three units ever reach a different star count than the bare factory value
No gameplay evidence; candidate is source reading plus mechanical checks only
